Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll apply the required `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect the rollout keyframes before touching the policy. I’ll stay within this Phase 2 workspace and the allowed evidence sources.

The skill requires a score-anchored visual comparison. I’m now reading the inherited guidance and every sampled observation/metric/log available, then I’ll compare the common prewarm sheet and the most informative rollout sheets before writing the required diagnosis.

The visual comparison is now clear: the replicated `0.25` lookahead anchor reaches the central wake sooner, while both tested “smoothing” changes delay corridor acquisition—`0.30` lookahead is the stronger regression, and closing-speed weakening also adds a late detour. I’m checking the exact observation contract next so the new candidate uses only supported, normalized body-frame feedback.

The skill-driven diagnosis rules out two tempting fixes: greater rate anticipation (`0.30`) and progress-conditioned bearing weakening (`0.32`) both preserve capture but delay useful-wake entry and worsen integrated distance. I’m recording a one-axis hypothesis before editing: retain the entire proven gait and test a shorter `0.20` bearing-rate lookahead, the local opposite of the falsified `0.30` change.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated: one policy only, with the tested change isolated to `0.20` rate lookahead. I’m invoking the workspace’s required checker next, then I’ll repair any schema/guidance issues it reports.

The guidance check passes. The contract checker itself did not run because the login profile references a missing workspace SSH directory and `julia` is not on that shell’s `PATH`; I’m resolving the local Julia executable and will rerun the exact non-CFD check directly.

All required checks now pass: reusable-guidance semantics, the Julia policy contract (using the workspace’s installed Julia directly), and the editable-boundary guard. I’m doing a final diff/whitespace audit to confirm only the single candidate plus the two required evidence files changed.

Completed exactly one candidate.

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:10): changed only bearing-rate lookahead from `0.25` to `0.20`.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:58): adds evidence-backed negative boundaries for longer lookahead and progress-conditioned steering weakening.

All required checks pass: guidance semantics, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-boundary validation. No CFD rollout was run.
